text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE on-call (pagerduty: sre_oncall). High error rate and latency spike detected in inference-serving: KV cache memory growth + continuous batching tail latency cliff. Affected: hosted inference fleet - model family 'redwood-small' and 'openchat-13b' (region: us-east-1). Autotrigger: autoscaler struggling; fallback traffic high. Please ack and triage.

sre_oncall: ack'd. looking now. can someone pull the recent cache metrics?

amelia: I'm seeing huge kv_cache.size growth on the 2k+ keys/minute scale starting ~08:02 UTC. Per-node mem up to 92%. Latency p50->p95 jump from 80ms to 1.2s.

cheng: I see continuous_batcher queue depth surging and batch latency unbounded. Maybe batcher is accumulating because of a mis-hash of prefixes -> a lot of unique cache keys, so caching not effective and batching can't aggregate.

miguel: adding logs from a sampled node: 
```
2024-05-05T08:05:12Z WARN kv_cache: miss key prompt_v2:9f3a1c... tokenizer_hash=7fff -> fallback miss
2024-05-05T08:05:12Z INFO batcher: created new batch size=1 target_model=redwood-small
2024-05-05T08:05:13Z ERROR inference: OOM while materializing KV cache, trying to GC
```

tara: noticing recent deploy 08:00 that bumped tokenizer-lib to 1.7.0 and template change for system prompts (product made minor drift). Could be hashing mismatch between tokenization used for cache key generation and runtime encoder.

eng-runtime: confirming: we rolled tokenizer 1.6.8 -> 1.7.0 in the runtime image at 08:00 (PR #4122). The cache key includes a tokenizer fingerprint right now. If the tokenizer outputs changed for same text, keys become unique -> cache explosion.

amelia: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback tokenizer to 1.6.8, 2) purge problematic cache prefixes, 3) throttle continuous batching or force batch flush to reduce memory pressure. Which do we prefer for fastest mitigation?

sre_oncall: let's do (2) + (3) now to buy time. rollback is heavier and will need deploy window. miguel can you run cache purge for prompt_v2 prefix across us-east-1? Also reduce batch size and set batch timeout lower.

miguel: running purge: `redwoodctl cache purge --region us-east-1 --prefix "prompt_v2:" --confirm`

miguel: purge started... issuing target nodes: 24. Will stream progress.

product-ops: FYI some live customers are reporting slower responses but no errors yet. I'll flag support to message any big customer hits.

cheng: applying batcher hotpatch to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 and batch_timeout 200ms -> 80ms to avoid long tail. Hotpatch command: 
```
redwoodctl config set --component continuous_batcher --region us-east-1 \
  --key max_batch_size=16 --key batch_timeout_ms=80
```

cheng: hotpatch applied to 12/24 nodes, monitoring...

miguel: purge progress 8/24 nodes done, memory dropping on those nodes. latency p95 reducing slightly.

incident-bot: incident severity escalated to SEV2 at 08:18 UTC due to widespread latency impact.

sre_oncall: good. keep purging and finish hotpatch across nodes. Next step: instrument to detect tokenizer mismatch by hashing token sequences rather than raw text. Need quick diagnostic to confirm root cause before rollback.

amelia: I ran a small diagnostic script to compare key generation between 1.6.8 and 1.7.0 on sample prompts. Results: same raw prompt -> tokenizer outputs different token lengths for ~12% of samples. That explains unique keys. Example: 
```
prompt: "Summarize the following..."
1.6.8 tokens: [101, 345, 990]
1.7.0 tokens: [101, 345, 990, 4]
key_v1 = hash("prompt_v2:" + text + ":tokv1:abcd") -> K1
key_v2 = hash("prompt_v2:" + text + ":tokv2:ef01") -> K2
```

tara: also found template drift: product changed system prompt wrapper to add a trailing newline in some templates, which would also change keys even with same tokenizer. So two orthogonal factors: tokenizer bump + template drift.

eng-runtime: for longer-term fix we should stop putting raw token sequences into the cache key. Instead include a canonicalized prompt fingerprint (normalizing whitespace) and a tokenizer-stable version. For now we'll add a flag to ignore tokenizer fingerprint so keys remain stable across minor tokenizer changes.

cheng: applied config rollback for key generation: `redwoodctl config set --component kv_cache --key include_tokenizer_fp=false` to avoid token-fingerprint variance. Rolling this to 24/24 nodes now.

miguel: all cache nodes now have include_tokenizer_fp=false. Doing a cluster-level gentle purge of prefixes created after 08:00: 
```
redwoodctl cache purge --since 2024-05-05T08:00:00Z --region us-east-1 --confirm
```

amelia: memory reclaiming across cluster, p95 latency back down to ~180ms, p50 85ms. Errors reduced. Good signal.

product-ops: sending status to support queue: "Mitigation in progress; tokenizer roll forward rolled back from cache keys; hotpatch applied to batcher; cluster purge underway. Customers may see transient latency improvement; no data loss."

miguel: kicking off canary rollback of tokenizer deploy to 1.6.8 for runtime image to remove long-term risk; will run canary on 2 nodes then full rollout if stable. Command: `deployctl rollback --image runtime:v1.7.0 --to runtime:v1.6.8 --canary 2`

eng-runtime: agree with canary. Also adding an instrumentation flag to log when token sequences differ across versions for the same input so we can detect future tokenizer drift in CI.

sre_oncall: useful postmortem actions: - revert include_tokenizer_fp removal once we have a proper schema for stable tokenizer-id, - add predeploy check to ensure tokenizer-only changes don't change cache key shape, - add a circuit breaker to continuous_batcher to avoid unbounded queue growth. I'll create the initial incident page.

incident-bot: handover scheduled: on-call shift to tara at 09:00 UTC. Please provide a 10-line summary before handoff.

tara: took over. quick summary: KV cache exploded due to tokenizer hash mismatch + template drift after 08:00 deploy -> cache key cardinality spike -> continuous batcher unable to form large batches -> memory pressure and tail latency. Mitigations: purge prompt_v2 keys, disable tokenizer fp in key gen, hotpatch batcher config, canary rollback tokenizer. Current status: cluster stable, p95 falling, monitoring.

amir (eng-runtime): adding follow-up ticket: ENG-1199 "Prompt cache key stability - remove tokenizer-sensitive hashing & canonicalization + CI gate". Assigned to eng-runtime, P1.

product-ops: flagged impacted customers for targeted follow-up if they saw degraded p95 > 1s during window.

sre_oncall: closing the page as mitigated but leaving incident open for postmortem and actions. If anyone sees re-regressions, ping this thread. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime: postmortem notes start: timeline, root cause (tokenizer bump + template drift), mitigations executed, config changes, follow-ups (ENG-1199, SRE-1203 circuit breaker for batcher, QA-45 predeploy tokenizer check).

incident-bot: incident severity de-escalated to SEV3 at 09:05 UTC.

amelia: thanks everyone. leaving logs and commands used in the incident channel snippet box.

(END)
